This appeal by the insurance company under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 26.02.2008 passed by Ist Additional MACT, Badwani in claim case no.158/06 seeking exoneration from liability and setting aside of the impugned award.

2. Brief facts of the case are that respondents no.1 & 2 preferred an application before the Tribunal alleging that their son Gauru @ Kishore when was travelling in the tractor trolley insured with the appellant, the driver/owner respondent no.l drove it rashly and negligently due to which Gauru fell United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kishore & 2 Ors. on 9 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125392290/
1 down and suffered injuries.

sentences.text: He died during treatment and alleging to be deceased at 20 years and his income Rs.5000/- per month, the compensation was claimed.
3. Respondent No.3 who is the owner and driver of the offending vehicle was proceeded ex-parte before the tribunal.

The appellant contested the case on the ground that false and fabricated case has been put forth as the deceased suffered injuries due to fall from the bullock card and not by the accident caused by the vehicle insured with the appellant.
4. Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence.

After hearing counsel for both parties the tribunal has held that the accident had caused by the vehicle insured with the appellant and awarded a compensation of Rs.2,96,000/- in favour of the claimants.

5. Being aggrieved by the impugned award, the insurance company has filed this appeal on the ground that the tribunal has erred in giving much stress on the prosecution documents but has failed to appreciate the evidence adduced on behalf of the appellant.

The tribunal has erred in not considering the fact that the documents relied upon by the claimants respondents more particularly first information report itself clearly shows that the deceased fell from the bullock cart.
So, the tribunal has wrongly awarded the compensation in favour of the claimants, hence prays for setting aside the impugned award.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

Learned counsel for the insurance company has argued that in the FIR Ex.P/1 it is mentioned that the deceased fell down from bullock cart, so it is a case of false implication of the offending vehicle for seeking compensation.
9. Perusal of Ex.P/.1 it is found that two Margs were registered in this case.

According to Ex.P/1,
first Marg was registered as Marg no.13/06 in which it was mentioned that the deceased fell down from the vehicle bearing registration no.MP-46-M-2427 and another Marg No.32/06 was registered on the basis of Marg no.048/06 that one person fell down from bullock cart and during treatment he died.

10. The police enquired the matter and after enquiry police filed the charge sheet Ex.P/7 against the offending vehicle tractor bearing registrarion No.MP-46-M-1005 and trolley bearing registration no.MP-46-M-1006.
11.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the FIR it is mentioned that the deceased fell down from bullock cart.
He further submits that the claimant cannot rely upon one part of the exhibited document and deny another part of the exhibited document.

It is true that in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Premlate Shukla and others - (2007) 13 SCC 476, the apex court has held that once a part of the exhibited document is relied upon by the party then the same party can't United India Insurance Co.Ltd. vs Kishore & 2 Ors.

2 say that he relies upon one part of the exhibited document and denies another part of the document.
In the present case it is true that FIR was not lodged by the claimant's side.
If the document was filed and exhibited by the claimant then he cannot deny part of the document.
In the present case Marg no.048/06 was not lodged by the claimant's side.
So it is the duty of the insurance company to call the witness who wrote it that the deceased fell down from the bullock cart.
This information was received from the hospital.

So the liability is upon the insurance company to prove it by calling the person who wrote it that the deceased fell down from the bullock cart but the insurance company has failed to adduce any evidence in this regard.
12. In the MLC report Ex.P/6 it is mentioned that the deceased received injuries in motor vehicle accident.
This MLC is dated 08.04.2006 and in the PM report the investigating officer has also written that the death of deceased was probably from tractor accident.
So considering the criminal documents it is found that the deceased fell down from tractor and not from the bullock cart.

Thus,
the tribunal has rightly given the finding that the deceased fell down from the tractor and not from the bullock cart.
This finding does not call for any interference by this Court in this appeal.
13. Accordingly, the appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
